summary: A shevuas hapikadon is when someone swears falsely that he does not have another person's things. It applies to everyone. If he did it on purpose, he pays back with an extra fifth and brings a korban asham.
stIntro: One who takes a false oath denying that he is in possession of an item that another deposited with him is liable to return the item with an additional one-fifth of its value and to bring a guilt-offering (see Leviticus 5:20–26).

chunks.st: he is liable to bring a guilt-offering and to pay restitution and an additional one-fifth, even if the oath was not administered in the presence of a court. And one is liable to bring an offering for intentionally taking a false oath on a deposit and for

summary: How a shevuas hapikadon works. If he swore falsely many times, he brings a korban for each one, because each time he could have admitted the truth.

chunks.en: How does a shevuas hapikadon work?
chunks.st: The mishna continues: What is the case of an oath on a deposit?

chunks.en: If someone said to him,
chunks.st: It is where the claimant said to the defendant:

chunks.en: "Give me my deposit that you have,"
chunks.st: Give me my deposit, which is in your possession, and the defendant replied:

chunks.en: and he answered, "I swear you have nothing with me,"
chunks.st: On my oath nothing of yours is in my possession;

chunks.he: אוֹ שֶׁאָמַר לוֹ אֵין לְךָ בְיָדִי,
chunks.en: or he said, "You have nothing with me,"

chunks.en: and the man said, "I make you swear,"

chunks.en: and he said "Amen,"
chunks.st: and the defendant said: Amen.

chunks.st: In either case this defendant is liable to bring a guilt-offering if he lied.

chunks.st: and the defendant falsely denied each claim, he is liable to bring a guilt-offering for each and every denial.

chunks.en: Because he could go back and admit.
chunks.explain: After each oath he could have admitted, so each oath is a new denial.
chunks.st: It is due to the fact that he is able to retract and confess after each oath and repay the claimant.
chunks.stMore: Since he did not do so, each oath is considered a separate denial of a monetary claim.

summary: If someone swore falsely that he did not do a terrible wrong to a man's daughter, Rabbi Shimon says he is patur, because that payment is a k'nas (a fine). The Sages say he is chayav, because some of what he must pay is for real damage.

chunks.en: If someone said, "You did a terrible wrong to my daughter, or tricked her,"
chunks.st: The mishna continues: If one accuses another: You raped or you seduced my daughter,

chunks.he: וְהוּא אוֹמֵר לֹא אָנַסְתִּי וְלֹא פִתִּיתִי.
chunks.en: and he said, "I did not do it, and I did not trick her,"
chunks.st: and the other says: I did not rape and I did not seduce your daughter, to which the father replied:

chunks.en: and the father said, "I make you swear,"
chunks.st: I administer an oath to you,

chunks.en: and he said "Amen,"
chunks.st: and the defendant said: Amen,

chunks.en: he is chayav. Rabbi Shimon says he is patur,
chunks.st: the defendant is liable to bring a guilt-offering if it is a false oath. Rabbi Shimon deems him exempt,

chunks.he: שֶׁאֵינוֹ מְשַׁלֵּם קְנָס עַל פִּי עַצְמוֹ.
chunks.en: because a person does not pay a k'nas just because he admits it himself.
chunks.st: since one does not pay a fine based on his own admission.
chunks.stMore: Had he confessed he would have been exempt from paying the fine; he is therefore not liable for his denial.

words.note: K'nas: a set payment the Torah adds as a punishment.

chunks.en: They said to him,
chunks.st: The Rabbis said to him:

chunks.en: Even though he does not pay
chunks.st: Even though he does not pay

chunks.en: the k'nas because he admits it himself,
chunks.st: the fine based on his own admission,

chunks.he: מְשַׁלֵּם בּשֶׁת וּפְגָם עַל פִּי עַצְמוֹ:
chunks.en: he does pay for shame and harm because he admits it himself.
chunks.explain: These are payments for real damage, not a fine, so his oath counts.
chunks.st: he does pay compensation for humiliation and compensation for degradation resulting from her being raped or seduced, which are monetary claims and not fines, based on his own admission.
chunks.stMore: He is therefore liable for a false oath, as he denied a monetary claim.

summary: The rule: if he would have to pay just by admitting it, a false oath makes him chayav a korban. If he would not pay by admitting (like a k'nas), he is patur.

chunks.en: If he said, "You stole my ox,"
chunks.st: Similarly, in a case where one person accuses another: You stole my ox,

chunks.en: and the other said, "I did not steal it,"
chunks.st: and the defendant says: I did not steal your ox, if the claimant replied:

chunks.en: and he said, "I make you swear,"
chunks.st: I administer an oath to you,

chunks.en: and he said "Amen,"
chunks.st: and the defendant said: Amen,

chunks.en: he is chayav.
chunks.st: he is liable
chunks.stMore: to pay for the ox due to the theft and to bring a guilt-offering if he lied, since by his oath he is denying that he owes the value of the ox that he would have to pay if he admitted to stealing it. But in a case where the claimant accuses the defendant of stealing the ox and slaughtering or selling it, and the defendant says:

chunks.he: גָּנַבְתִּי אֲבָל לֹא טָבַחְתִּי וְלֹא מָכָרְתִּי,
chunks.en: If he said, "I stole it, but I did not slaughter it or sell it,"
chunks.explain: A thief who slaughtered or sold the ox pays five times; that extra is a k'nas.
chunks.st: I stole the ox, but I did not slaughter or sell it, and this is a lie, if the claimant replied:

chunks.en: and he said, "I make you swear,"
chunks.st: I administer an oath to you,

chunks.en: and he said "Amen,"
chunks.st: and he said: Amen, then the defendant is

chunks.en: he is patur.
chunks.st: exempt
chunks.stMore: from the fivefold payment for slaughtering or selling another’s ox, since it is a fine. If the claimant says:

chunks.en: If he said, "Your ox killed my ox,"
chunks.st: Your ox killed my ox,

chunks.en: and the other said, "It did not kill it,"
chunks.st: and the defendant lies and says: It did not kill your ox, to which the claimant replied:

chunks.en: and he said, "I make you swear,"
chunks.st: I administer an oath to you,

chunks.en: and he said "Amen,"
chunks.st: and he said: Amen,

chunks.en: he is chayav.
chunks.st: then he is liable for his false oath.

chunks.en: If he said, "Your ox killed my servant,"
chunks.explain: For a servant, the owner of the ox pays thirty shekels, which is a k'nas.
chunks.st: Your ox killed my Canaanite slave and you are therefore liable to pay me a fine of thirty shekels,

chunks.en: and the other said, "It did not kill him,"
chunks.st: and he lies and says: It did not kill your slave, to which the claimant replied:

chunks.en: and he said, "I make you swear,"
chunks.st: I administer an oath to you,

chunks.en: and he said "Amen,"
chunks.st: and he said: Amen,

chunks.en: he is patur.
chunks.st: then he is exempt, because payment for the slave is a fine.

chunks.en: If he said to him,
chunks.st: If the claimant said to him:

chunks.en: "You hurt me and gave me a wound,"
chunks.st: You injured me and caused me a wound,

chunks.en: and the other said, "I did not hurt you,
chunks.st: and the defendant says: I did not injure

chunks.en: and I did not give you a wound,"
chunks.st: you and I did not cause you a wound, to which the claimant replies:

chunks.en: and he said, "I make you swear,"
chunks.st: I administer an oath to you,

chunks.en: and he said "Amen,"
chunks.st: and he said: Amen,

chunks.en: he is chayav.
chunks.st: he is liable.

chunks.en: If his servant said to him,
chunks.st: But if one’s Canaanite slave said to him:

chunks.he: הִפַּלְתָּ אֶת שִׁנִּי וְסִמִּיתָ אֶת עֵינִי,
chunks.en: "You knocked out my tooth," or "You blinded my eye,"
chunks.explain: Then the master must set the servant free.
chunks.st: You knocked out my tooth, or: You blinded my eye, and you are therefore required to emancipate me,

chunks.he: וְהוּא אוֹמֵר לֹא הִפַּלְתִּי וְלֹא סִמִּיתִי,
chunks.en: and he said, "I did not knock it out, and I did not blind it,"
chunks.st: and he says: I did not knock out your tooth, or: I did not blind your eye, to which the slave replies:

chunks.en: and the servant said, "I make you swear,"
chunks.st: I administer an oath to you,

chunks.en: and he said "Amen,"
chunks.st: and he said: Amen,

chunks.en: he is patur.
chunks.st: he is exempt
chunks.stMore: from bringing a guilt-offering even though he lied, since the obligation to emancipate one’s slave in these cases is a penalty.

chunks.en: This is the rule:
chunks.st: This is the principle:

chunks.en: Whenever a person would pay because he admitted it himself,
chunks.st: For any claim that the defendant would have to pay based on his own admission,

chunks.en: he is chayav.
chunks.st: he is liable
chunks.stMore: to bring a guilt-offering for taking a false oath concerning that claim.

chunks.he: וְשֶׁאֵינוֹ מְשַׁלֵּם עַל פִּי עַצְמוֹ, פָּטוּר:
chunks.en: And whenever he would not pay because he admitted it himself, he is patur.
chunks.st: And for any claim that he would not pay based on his own admission but would pay only by the testimony of witnesses, he is exempt
chunks.stMore: from bringing a guilt-offering for taking a false oath concerning that claim.
